findings.title: Password check can be bypassed when backupCode is used with totpCode
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts the password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121: `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`). The backup-code branch at line 131 (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`) does not verify the password and does not verify the totpCode. An attacker can therefore send credentials with email + any non-empty totpCode (e.g. "123456") + a backup code, causing the password check to be skipped while authentication succeeds on the backup code alone. This turns the second factor into a password replacement and allows login without knowing the password via direct calls to the credentials provider, whereas the UI normally still submits the password.

findings.title: Unsafe replaceAll on backupCode assumes string
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 the code does `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` after only checking truthiness of `req.body.backupCode`. If the client sends a non-string value (array, object, number) the call throws TypeError, resulting in an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode response. The same pattern exists in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts line 144. Request bodies must be type-validated/normalized (String(), trim, case handling) before calling string methods.

findings.title: Throwing instead of returning 500 in API handler
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts lines 51, 77, 82 the handler does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when the encryption key is missing or the 2FA secret is inconsistent. Inside a Next.js API route without a try/catch this produces an unhandled exception/HTML 500 instead of the JSON `{error: ...}` contract used everywhere else in the file, breaking clients that call `response.json()` and potentially leaking stack traces. It should `return res.status(500).json({ error: ... })` like setup.ts does.

findings.title: Default-exported component misnamed TwoFactor
findings.body: In apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx line 7 the component is declared as `export default function TwoFactor` even though the file defines the BackupCode input and is imported as `BackupCode`. There are now two different default exports both named TwoFactor (this file and TwoFactor.tsx). It works at runtime but breaks displayName/debugging, confuses stack traces and React DevTools, and invites wrong imports. It should be renamed to `BackupCode`.
